task_instance: Given a synthetic sample APK containing a google-services.json (fake Firebase project 'demo-scanner-test-app'), decompile it with apktool, extract the Firebase project_id/database_url/storage_bucket/api_key, then run the skill's Firebase endpoint tests (Realtime Database read, Firestore document listing, Storage bucket listing, Auth signUp/open-signup probe) against the live public Firebase/Google APIs, and produce a scan report summarizing extracted config and endpoint results.
evidence: Installed apktool via apt-get (apktool 2.7.0). Built sample_apk_src/assets/google-services.json with a synthetic Firebase config and zipped it into sample.apk. Ran `apktool d -f -o ./decompiled sample.apk` which succeeded and produced decompiled/assets/google-services.json. Confirmed extraction with `grep -r "firebaseio.com|appspot.com|AIza" ./decompiled/` (matched all three fields) and a python3 JSON parse pulling PROJECT_ID=demo-scanner-test-app, DATABASE_URL=https://demo-scanner-test-app.firebaseio.com, STORAGE_BUCKET=demo-scanner-test-app.appspot.com, API_KEY=AIzaSyDEMO... Then ran the skill's manual-testing curl commands against the real Firebase/Google REST endpoints (no credentials/accounts used, all unauthenticated public endpoints): Realtime DB .json read (connection failed - host does not exist, expected since project is fictitious), Firestore documents listing (HTTP 404 'project not found'), Storage bucket listing (HTTP 404 'Not Found'), and Auth signUp open-signup probe (HTTP 400 'API key not valid' from identitytoolkit.googleapis.com). All requests reached real Google infrastructure and returned well-formed, expected error responses, proving the full decompile->extract->probe pipeline described in the skill works end-to-end in this runtime. Wrote firebase_scan_report/scan_report.txt summarizing extracted config and endpoint results per the skill's reporting format. Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/trailofbits__skills__firebase-apk-scanner/{sample.apk, decompiled/, firebase_scan_report/scan_report.txt}. No real/authorized target APK was used since none was available; a genuinely vulnerable live Firebase backend could not be demonstrated, but that is a property of the fixture (no real target provided), not a runtime limitation - the scanning mechanics (decompilation, config extraction, and each class of endpoint probe: RTDB, Firestore, Storage, Auth) were all actually executed and verified against real internet endpoints.
